claims.text: General rule: in most states, people under 18 cannot legally consent to medical care, so most nonemergency care needs a parent's or guardian's consent.
claims.quote: In most states, children below the age of 18 years do not have the legal capacity to give medical consent. Therefore, for most nonemergency medical decisions affecting minors, medical care cannot proceed without a parent’s or guardian’s consent.

claims.text: Exceptions: emancipated minors can consent to all care, and in most states minors can consent to certain services (eg, STI treatment, birth control prescriptions) without a parent; check the state's law.
claims.quote: First, emancipated minors can consent to all medical treatments on their own behalf. Second, in most states, minors can consent to certain medical treatments (eg, treatment of sexually transmitted infections, prescriptions for birth control, treatment of drug and substance use, mental health treatment) without parental permission. Individual state law must be consulted.

claims.text: Title X clinics: Title X family planning projects may not require a parent's or guardian's consent to serve a minor, and staff may not notify a parent before or after a minor gets services.
claims.quote: Title X projects may not require consent of parents or guardians for the provision of services to minors, nor can any Title X project staff notify a parent or guardian before or after a minor has requested and/or received Title X family planning services.

claims.text: Title X confidentiality: what a patient shares must not be disclosed without the patient's documented consent, except as needed to provide services or as required by law.
claims.quote: All information as to personal facts and circumstances obtained by the project staff about individuals receiving services must be held confidential and must not be disclosed without the individual's documented consent, except as may be necessary to provide services to the patient or as required by law

claims.text: Insurance disclosures: Title X clinics must tell patients when their information could reach a policyholder other than themselves.
claims.quote: Recipient must inform the client of any potential for disclosure of their confidential health information to policyholders where the policyholder is someone other than the client.

notes.issue: Claim carried an illustration ('eg, a parent's insurance') not in the quoted text.
notes.resolution: Illustration removed so the claim is quote-bound; re-check passed.
